vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vikunja-task-api
Version: 2.1.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the Vikunja task management API. It provides a helper script (vikunja.sh) and comprehensive documentation (SKILL.md) for managing projects, tasks, and labels. The code uses standard tools like curl and jq, handles authentication correctly via environment variables (VIKUNJA_TOKEN or credentials), and contains no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill’s requests, environment variables, and included script are consistent with a Vikunja API client; nothing in the files attempts unrelated access, but there are minor provenance/metadata inconsistencies you should verify before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim a full Vikunja v2 API integration and the SKILL.md plus vikunja.sh implement exactly that (curl/jq calls to $VIKUNJA_URL, token or username/password auth, endpoints for projects/tasks/labels etc.). Required binaries (curl, jq) and env vars (VIKUNJA_URL, VIKUNJA_TOKEN optional username/password) match the stated purpose. Note: package metadata shows inconsistent owner IDs and minor version/titles (SKILL.md mentions v2.2.2 in its header text while manifest/version fields are 2.1.0); provenance is unclear.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script limit actions to interacting with the Vikunja API (GET/PUT/POST/DELETE to $VIKUNJA_URL/api/v1). They do not read unrelated system files, other env vars, or send data to endpoints outside the configured VIKUNJA_URL. The script will request a token from the configured Vikunja instance if username/password are provided — this is expected behavior for obtaining auth.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only plus an included helper script). No external downloads, archives, or installers are declared. The included bash script is readable and calls only curl/jq and the configured VIKUNJA_URL.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests only VIKUNJA_URL and (primarily) VIKUNJA_TOKEN, with optional VIKUNJA_USERNAME/VIKUNJA_PASSWORD for token acquisition. These are proportionate to a Vikunja API client. No unrelated credentials or secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It does not persist credentials itself beyond reading env variables at runtime. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal), but not combined with other risky behaviors here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward Vikunja API helper. Before installing: (1) Verify the skill source/provenance — the registry metadata and _meta.json show inconsistent owner/version fields and the skill source is listed as unknown. (2) Only point VIKUNJA_URL to a trusted Vikunja instance. (3) Prefer creating and supplying a scoped API token (VIKUNJA_TOKEN) rather than handing over your username/password; if you must provide username/password the script will POST them to the configured VIKUNJA_URL to obtain a token. (4) Review the included vikunja.sh yourself (it’s small and human-readable) and confirm its behavior is acceptable. (5) If you later find the skill untrusted, revoke the API token in your Vikunja account. If you want higher assurance, ask the publisher for source repository links or a verified owner identity before use.
